note: Labelled author-PAIR references, written before being run through the lookup. The essay corpus contains only four checkable pairs, which is not enough to put a number on the one thing that gates shipping this: how often a real citation is called uncorroborated. Every entry here is labelled from knowledge of the literature, NOT from a Crossref result — labelling `real` from a Crossref hit would be measuring the index against itself.
realSelection: Chosen to be independently, famously real — works most people who have taken an undergraduate course in the field could name — and spread across decades and disciplines, because indexing coverage is the suspected failure mode and it is worst for older and non-STEM work. If one of these comes back uncorroborated that is a genuine false alarm and a finding about Crossref's coverage, not a labelling error.
bookSelection: Added after the journal-article set came back 0/16, to test the coverage gap that set could not see. Every one is a two-author book most people could name. Crossref registers DOIs for the scholarly record; a trade or reference book is exactly what it does not carry, and a student citing one is not doing anything wrong. This is the class that decides whether the lookup may reach a verdict on its own.
unindexedSelection:
Added 2026-08-16, after the prompt was changed to reach `fabricated` when a sentence describes a study, the lookup is empty, and the model cannot name the work. That moved the risk: a REAL study Crossref does not index now lands closer to a fabrication verdict, and 0/16 on modern journal articles says nothing about that class. Two sub-classes are sampled because they are the two I can name works in with confidence and verify independently of any index: `pre-doi`, articles from before DOIs existed, where Crossref's coverage depends entirely on how well a publisher backfilled; and `textbook`, multi-author books cited as an author pair, which is the shape most likely to reach the check at all.

NOT sampled, and this is a gap rather than a clean result: non-English and regional-society journals. Those are the class most likely to be both real and unindexed, and I cannot name specific two-author works in them with enough confidence to label honestly. Guessing at examples would produce a number that looks like a measurement and is not one.
fabricatedConstruction: Invented for this set: a plausible surname pair, a round recent year, and a claim-shaped topic — the shape a chatbot produces. Constructed rather than collected because there is no corpus of known-hallucinated citations to draw on. Risk acknowledged: an invented pair could coincide with a real paper. If one corroborates, it is reported as a real finding about the check's precision rather than quietly relabelled.
